To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inactivation kinetics of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens alpha-amaylase is strongly dependent on the state (bound or free) of calcium ion and that the calcium binding to the enzyme is an enthalpically favorable process.

the irreversible thermal inactivation of Bacillus amylaoliquefaciens a-amylase was apparently followed by a first-order kinetic and the inactivation was dependent on the state and the binding parameters of calcium ion.
the irreversible thermal inactivation of alpha-amylase is dependent on the state and extent of calcium ion binding and that the thermodynamic properties of calcium binding are strongly enthalpic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an understanding of the thermodynamic and kinetic aspects of calcium ion binding and the thermal inactivation of alpha-amylase.
the inactivation kinetics and thermodynamic properties of the Bacillus amylolyiquefaciens alpha- amylase.
the inactivation kinetics of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens alpha-amyalase in the absence and presence of calcium ions and with the thermodynamics of the calcium ion binding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium binding to the alpha-amylase protein is a prerequisite for the stabilization of its structure against the thermal denaturation.
the calcium ion binding is the primary cause of the inactivation resistance.
the enzyme is stabilized by calcium ion binding in the inactivation process and the stabilization is mainly enthalpically driven.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inactivation kinetic study is a powerful tool to determine the calcium-binding parameters of the enzyme protein.
the calcium ion binding is a prerequisite step for the inactivation of alpha-amylase and thus the inactivating process is a two-step reaction.

the calcium-binding parameter of the enzyme is a key factor for the thermal inactivation and that the inactivation kinetic model can be used to estimate the calcium-binding parameters of alpha-amylase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inactivation of the enzyme is highly correlated with the calcium ion binding.
the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters of the enzyme are strongly affected by the calcium binding and the calcium binding is highly enthalpy-driven and enthalpy-entropy compensating.
the thermodynamic parameters obtained from the kinetic data are useful for the interpretation of the thermodynamics of protein unfolding and the calcium binding to the enzyme.
